findings.summary: N20 cannot reach PASSED: its graph verification command `python3 plans/27_langgraph_curriculum_factory_remediation/controller/check_forbidden_production_refs.py` defaults to --scope all, which includes the retired_provider_test_scan over the whole tests/runtime tree. Six migration-affected active test files carrying gemini/google terms are owned by later nodes and are outside N20's write set: tests/runtime/test_plan26_cli.py, test_plan26_deterministic_nodes.py, test_plan26_egress.py, test_run_curriculum.py (N30_PREFLIGHT_EGRESS), test_plan26_topology.py (N40_INTEGRATION_OWNERSHIP), test_plan26_persistence.py (N50_EVIDENCE_AUDIT_CONTROLS). The identical bare command is also N30's, N40's and N50's verification, so the scan can first exit 0 only after N50 completes; N20, N30 and N40 are each unsatisfiable as written. Owner: the implementation graph's verification list (with the controller invocation N10 built). Minimal fix: give N20/N30/N40/N50 `--scope production` plus a scope that covers only their own owned test paths, and keep the bare `--scope all` form at N60_ADVERSARIAL_REGRESSION, which already owns the whole-tree pytest denominator. Evidence: 30_scan_scope_all.log, 32_scan_violation_owners.log.

N20 cannot express the corrected provider assignment inside its own write set. Spec v2 s7.4 requires the authorization classes `anthropic` (M01-M04/M06/M08) and `openai` (M05/M07) and forbids any `google` class. transport.CliTransport.execute() passes the frozen route's `provider` field directly into egress.authorize_subprocess_transmission, and the allowlist that decides which provider names exist (PROVIDERS and PROVIDER_DATA_CLASSES) lives in runtime/langgraph_factory/egress.py, owned by N30_PREFLIGHT_EGRESS. Constructing an AuthorizationRecord with provider `anthropic` raises AuthorizationDenied('unknown_provider'). Writing `provider: anthropic` into the N20-owned config/model_jobs.v1.yaml therefore breaks every end-to-end transport test the moment it is written, and keeping `provider: openai` on a Claude job would authorize anthropic-class data under the openai class, which s7.4 forbids. Owner: N30_PREFLIGHT_EGRESS. Required egress change: rename PROVIDER_DATA_CLASSES['openai'] (authoring classes) to 'anthropic' and PROVIDER_DATA_CLASSES['google'] (review classes) to 'openai', set PROVIDERS accordingly, and drop the *.googleapis.com model endpoints from MODEL_API_HOSTS. N20's own runtime/langgraph_factory/schemas/internal_authorization_receipt.schema.json provider enum must change in the same atomic step. Evidence: 40_egress_provider_coupling.log.

Spec v2 s7.2's pinned Claude invocation shape is factually wrong against the installed CLI and cannot be implemented literally. Proven live on 2026-08-13 against claude 2.1.231: (a) `--json-schema output.schema.json` is rejected — the flag takes the schema inline as a JSON string, not a file path ('--json-schema is not valid JSON: JSON Parse error: Unexpected identifier "output"'); (b) passing the package's own job schema inline is also rejected while it carries its draft 2020-12 $schema reference ('no schema with key or ref "https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema"'), so the transport must strip $schema before transmission. The workspace copy of output.schema.json remains correct for hashing and for post-hoc jsonschema validation, but it is not what the CLI consumes. Evidence: 21_claude_json_schema_path_rejected.log, 22_claude_meta_schema_ref_rejected.log.

Spec v2 s7.1 and s7.2 contradict each other for Claude jobs: s7.1 says the request instruction 'identifies only the staged filenames' while s7.2 pins `--tools ""`. Proven live: with `--tools ""` the session init event reports tools ['StructuredOutput'] only, so the Claude worker has no file-reading tool and cannot open authorized_input.json or any staged artifact in the workspace that --add-dir scopes. As written, a Claude job would receive its prompt text and nothing else. Resolving this needs an approved decision — either transmit the authorized projection inline in the instruction, or allow exactly one read-only file tool scoped to --add-dir — and N20 must not invent it. Owner: the job contract / staged boundary (spec, then N30's staged-input path). Evidence: 23_claude_stream_json_identity_events.log.

Executed-model identity for the Claude route is observable and the extraction mechanism is now proven, not assumed. `claude --print --output-format stream-json --verbose` on 2.1.231 emits a system/init event carrying "model", assistant events carrying message.model with parent_tool_use_id null, and a final result event carrying structured_output plus modelUsage keyed by executed model id with canonicalModel and provider (observed "firstParty"). This is a strict machine-readable superset of what `--output-format json` gives and is the s7.2-sanctioned alternative event source. Note the plain `--output-format json` envelope's modelUsage map is NOT single-entry — a probe recorded claude-haiku-4-5 alongside the requested claude-sonnet-5 — so a gemini-style 'exactly one model' extractor over modelUsage would fail spuriously; the per-turn assistant message.model is the unambiguous signal. Evidence: 20_claude_version.log, 23_claude_stream_json_identity_events.log.

Containment gap observed live for a later node: `--setting-sources ""` did not suppress MCP server loading. The session init event listed three claude.ai MCP servers (Google Drive, Gmail, Google Calendar, all status needs-auth). They were unauthenticated and no tool was exposed under `--tools ""`, so nothing was reachable in this probe, but s7.2's claim that --setting-sources "" 'prevents the invocation from reading ... MCP configuration' is not fully borne out. Owner: N30_PREFLIGHT_EGRESS capability proof and N70's live proof. Evidence: 23_claude_stream_json_identity_events.log.

N20's pytest verification already fails on the unmodified tree, independently of anything N20 would change: tests/runtime/test_plan26_transport.py::test_capability_probes_read_the_real_local_toolchain asserts prove_capability('model_cli_identity') == PASS, and the probe resolves every CLI named by the frozen registry, which still includes `gemini`. No gemini executable is installed on this host, so the probe returns MISSING. 315 passed, 1 failed, 6 skipped. The provider migration removes the gemini route and both remaining drivers (claude 2.1.231, codex) are installed, so this failure is expected to clear once the migration lands. Evidence: 60_pytest_n20_baseline.log.

TEST step 1 and step 10 satisfied: the eight-job table was built from spec v2 s6.3/s7.1-s7.4 plus the user-approved USER_DECISION_REQUIRED-01 resolution, with role, mutability, provider family, subscription driver, model, effort, input boundary, output schema, identity claim and failure disposition resolved for all of M01-M08 and no unresolved field. It records M01/M06/M08 = claude-sonnet-5 xhigh, M02/M03/M04 = claude-sonnet-5 high, M05/M07 = gpt-5.6-sol xhigh, and the family-mismatch-is-system rule for M05/M07. Evidence: 11_eight_job_conformance_table.log.

No file in N20's declared write set was modified. Because N20-F01 and N20-F02 make a PASSED outcome unreachable before other nodes act, and because a half-applied provider migration would leave the runtime unable to authorize any model job at all (F02), the migration was not partially applied. changed_files is empty and `git status --porcelain` still shows only the admitted N00/N10 scaffold. The corrected table, the proven Claude identity mechanism and the two evidenced spec-shape defects (F03, F04) are recorded so the next N20 attempt does not have to rediscover them.
